ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every UBO, director, officer and beneficial signatory against: (i) FINTRAC's PCMLTFA Politically Exposed Persons definition (heads of state, cabinet-level officials, senior public office holders, and their family members and close associates); (ii) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iii) domestic Alberta Corporate Registry refusal and name-clearance records; (iv) OFAC SDN list; and (v) UK HMT Consolidated Sanctions List, given the Stripe and Apple IAP payment-rail nexus to the United States and the United Kingdom. Any PEP, sanctions or adverse-media match automatically escalates to enhanced due diligence and requires written clearance from compliance counsel before name reservation or incorporation may proceed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry operated by Service Alberta, with mandatory submission of a current NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report prepared through authorized NUANS service providers (nuans.com national system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English letters (Latin script) and must be capable of exact reproduction and search in the NUANS database; French-language and bilingual names are permitted but not mandatory at the Alberta provincial level; the name must consist of a distinctive element and a legal element; for an unlimited liability corporation the legal element must be 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or the abbreviation 'ULC'; punctuation and numerical restrictions apply under the Business Corporations Act Name Regulation, Alta. Reg. 101/2001
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On receipt of a name rejection notice, counsel must within 15 days: (1) obtain a fresh or topped-up NUANS report and re-submit a revised primary and reserve name; (2) file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act Name Regulation, attaching trademark registration certificates, common-law use evidence and any professional regulator consents; (3) if the Director affirms the refusal, file a judicial-review application in the Alberta Court of King's Bench within 30 days of the decision; a further 90-day NUANS hold may be restored at the Director's discretion upon demonstrated good faith in the revised filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for this low-risk ISIC 6201 fintech SaaS on condition that the Alberta registered office is a physical street address in Alberta at which service of process can be effected during normal business hours and that is operated by a licensed registered agent. A purely virtual arrangement without substantive operational presence may increase Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) residency-recharacterization risk and GST/HST audit exposure; therefore a contractually substantive office relationship with the agent and demonstrable board/management substance in Canada is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated 3-5% annual probability of a registry compliance inspection for a low-risk software entity; estimated 5-10% probability of a CRA tax-return or GST/HST desk or on-site audit for a virtual-office ULC with limited substance and a foreign ultimate beneficial owner, increasing if annual revenue volume is material or the entity books significant B2B revenue through Canadian payment infrastructure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, Part 2 (Incorporation) and s. 15.1 (unlimited liability corporations); Business Corporations Regulations, Alta Reg 119/2001, Form 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for Alberta ULCs; shares may be issued without par value. For the fintech portfolio-tracking SaaS, settlement funds flow via Stripe and Apple IAP and are not held by the corporation, so no deposit trust or capitalization is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscriptions of the incorporator-shareholders for the aggregate number of common shares approved at this meeting, such shares to be issued as fully paid and non-assessable in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation; and be it further RESOLVED, that the registered records office of the Corporation shall be located at [Registered Office Address] in Alberta, and the records at that place shall be maintained pursuant to the Business Corporations Act; and be it further RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer of the Corporation, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board until replaced by ordinary resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an authorized Corporate Registry Access service provider or Service Alberta corporate online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS corporate name search request limited to Alberta and Canada. Ensure the proposed legal name includes the term 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', or the French equivalent. Obtain the NUANS report and reserve the name with the Corporate Registry for 90 days. If a numbered company is preferred, this step may be skipped.
required_dossiers: completed corporate name request cover sheet
NUANS compatibility report not older than 90 days
signed name consent if the name contains a personal or corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a second-choice name within the same reservation period or proceed as a numbered company. If the NUANS report expires, a fresh report is required before filing incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporation counsel or Alberta Corporate Registry pre-filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, first directors, and the mandatory statement that the corporation is an unlimited liability corporation. Complete the prescribed Form 1 and any consent forms. Obtain signed consent of the proposed shareholders to their unlimited statutory liability. Obtain landlord or occupier consent for the proposed registered records office.
required_dossiers: consent to act as first director
registered office address and landlord or occupier consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If pre-filing comments or desk review requests are issued, revise the Articles and resubmit before paying the incorporation fee. Any substantive change requires a fresh consent to act as director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; online filing portal or authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation, NUANS report, director consents, shareholder consents, and registered office consent through the Corporate Registry electronic filing system or at an authorized registry agent. Pay the prescribed filing fee. Upon successful review, the Registry endorses the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Domestic signatures generally need not be notarized, but foreign signatories should have signatures commissioned or notarized.
required_dossiers: NUANS report or name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registry Notice within the stated deadline, correct the relevant schedules, and re-file. Late or unanswered queries require a fresh incorporation filing and additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organization and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors and incorporator; Alberta Corporate Registry for subsequent director, officer, or registered office filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting and adopt the first board resolution covering acceptance of share subscriptions, adoption or authorization of bylaws, designation of the registered records office, appointment of officers, and issuance of share certificates. Record the share ledger and minute book. File any changes to directors, officers, or registered office with the Corporate Registry within the statutory notification period if they differ from the filed Articles.
required_dossiers: corporate minute book and first board resolution
notice of change of registered office or notice of directors and officers if post-filing changes occur
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a required notification is late, file an application for late acceptance or correction with the Corporate Registry. Confirm the annual return date immediately to avoid administrative dissolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Program Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta tax registration administered through the single CRA window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the corporate income tax account using the Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Registry profile. Register for GST/HST if taxable SaaS or app-in-app sales exceed CAD 30,000 in any four consecutive calendar quarters, or voluntarily to recover input tax credits. If employees will be hired, open a payroll deductions program account and register with the Alberta Workers' Compensation Board.
required_dossiers: ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210 business activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA cannot verify the corporate record, provide a Corporate Registry profile report. If the Business Number is delayed, request an administrative confirmation letter from Service Alberta and escalate through the CRA Business Enquiries line.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Occupancy or Fire Clearance if Applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Alberta municipal licensing authority and municipal fire inspection service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the corporation will maintain a physical office, a home office, or no office. If a commercial office is leased, apply for the municipal business licence, obtain the fire safety inspection certificate, and post the building occupancy load certificate required by the Alberta Building Code. For a pure virtual cloud portfolio-tracking operation, no manufacturing, industrial, or environmental permit is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning or occupancy inspection fails, submit a compliance plan to the municipal licensing authority or relocate to a compliant premises. Obtain a temporary occupancy certificate while remedial works are completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None engaged; no industrial licence-granting board applies to a digital cloud software and portfolio-tracking activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required; a municipal business licence may be required only if a physical office is established.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt; no physical works requiring registration or approval under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; no process wastewater, VOC emissions, or regulated waste streams are generated by the cloud portfolio-tracking application. Any leased office must comply with municipal sewer bylaws, Alberta waste management obligations, and applicable data-centre lessor environmental permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any leased premises: municipal fire safety certification, building structural load clearance for office fittings and server equipment under the Alberta Building Code, and an Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code workplace clearance. No civil defense or industrial production clearance is triggered by the software activity itself.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portal: CRA My Business Account; registration via Business Registration Online (BRO). For Alberta corporate income tax, the CRA administers under a federal-provincial tax collection agreement; the Alberta provincial tax authority is Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST account and Canada Revenue Agency program accounts. Apply via CRA Business Registration Online or file Form RC1. Supporting documentation: certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, registered office information, director/officer identification, foreign entity registration documents, and proof of authority for the individual completing the application. If no Canadian director or physical presence, the CRA may require a representative or agent. No separate Alberta corporate tax registration because Alberta corporate income tax is collected federally, but the entity must file a provincial corporate tax return in respect of income allocated to Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An Alberta ULC is generally taxed as a corporation under the federal Income Tax Act; however, under subsection 34(2) of the Income Tax Act, a ULC may elect to be treated as a partnership for Canadian tax purposes if all members are resident in Canada or are certain non-resident corporations (per the statutory conditions). This election is available only to Canadian resident member corporations/partnerships, and is generally unavailable for a ULC with U.S. individual shareholders. For U.S. federal tax purposes, an Alberta ULC is a per se corporation under U.S. Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-2(b)(8)(i)(A), so it cannot make a check-the-box election to be disregarded. No other check-the-box mechanism exists under Canadian law. Hybrid mismatch rules (sections 18.4 and 18.5 of the Income Tax Act) may apply to deny deductions on payments giving rise to hybrid financial instrument or hybrid transfer benefits; no affirmative election prevents these rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada). Alberta does not levy provincial sales tax; only the federal 5% GST applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters; only supplies made in Canada count toward the threshold for non-residents carrying on business in Canada. A non-resident supplying digital services to Canadian customers must register if the threshold is met, unless the supply is zero-rated and the non-resident is not carrying on business in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime is currently mandated for GST/HST in Canada. E-invoicing is permitted and must satisfy CRA record-keeping requirements under the Excise Tax Act, including supplier name, GST/HST registration number, invoice date, description of supply, amount, and tax charged. Voluntary e-invoicing standards (e.g., Peppol) are accepted. No fiscal device or pre-approval is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant may zero-rate a supply of a service under Section 7 of Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and is not present in Canada at the time the service is supplied, and the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed. For software-based financial portfolio tracking services delivered over the cloud, zero-rating applies if the customer is a non-resident individual or unregistered non-resident business and the service does not relate to Canadian-situated property. The supplier must obtain documentary evidence of non-residency, including IP geolocation, billing address, payment card country, and customer attestation where available.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (e.g., Canadian Export Reporting System/CERS) only if tangible goods are exported; for pure digital services, no customs export declaration is required
Commercial invoice or service agreement identifying the non-resident recipient and Canadian supplier
Evidence of payment inflow, including SWIFT/MT103 or payment processor statements from Stripe/Apple
Non-resident status evidence: customer attestation, certificate of residence, or jurisdiction-specific tax residency certificate
IP address/geolocation logs and billing address evidencing the customer is outside Canada
GST/HST registration status confirmation that the recipient is not registered under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess within the normal four-year reassessment period (or longer in cases of misrepresentation or fraud) to deny zero-rating, requiring remittance of 5% GST on the revenue, plus interest and penalties. Penalties under sections 280 and 285 of the Excise Tax Act may apply where a registrant knowingly makes false statements: the amount can be up to 25% of the tax sought, plus fines and imprisonment on conviction. Input tax credits claimed on expenses attributable to the zero-rated supply may be clawed back if the zero-rating is overturned. The CRA scrutinizes cross-border digital services using payment processor data; failure to substantiate non-resident recipient status or failure to remit within the statutory period can result in assessment, collection actions, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Canadian foreign exchange is market-determined under the Bank of Canada Act and Currency Act. Supervisory oversight for banks and FX dealers is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while transaction monitoring and cross-border reporting are enforced by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully liberalized currency régime consistent with IMF Article VIII. Both current account payments (e.g., royalties, dividends, service fees) and capital account transfers (e.g., equity injections, loan repayments, derivative settlements) are freely convertible into CAD and outbound foreign currency without prior exchange-control approval. Profit remittance from an Alberta ULC is subject solely to Canadian taxation, primarily Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends (statutorily 25%, reduced under applicable income tax treaties) and, where applicable, branch tax or withholding on deemed receipts. No regulatory exchange-rate restriction or conversion limit applies to the repatriation of business profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose statutory export proceeds surrender timelines or mandatory conversion ratios. Receipts denominated in foreign currency may be retained, converted, or repatriated freely under the floating exchange rate régime. Reporting obligations apply only under FINTRAC for cross-border electronic fund transfers (EFTs) of CAD $10,000 or more within a 24-hour period, and under Statistics Canada’s International Transactions Reporting System for balance-of-payments purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD multi-currency with USD sub-account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Montreal (BMO, Bank of Montreal operating as BMO Bank of Montreal)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are not recognized as deposit-taking banking entities under the Bank Act; they fall outside the Canadian regulatory perimeter and cannot provide insured or fully regulated clearing facilities for a ULC treasury. A foreign EMI may operate in relation to Canada only as an unregulated payment provider, creating material settlement risk, FX custody risk, and FINTRAC-reporting gaps. For strategic treasury purposes, such providers are acceptable only as ancillary collection channels for operating revenue; all liquidity, hedging, and capital movements must be executed through OSFI-regulated Schedule I banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote opening is permitted but subject to enhanced due diligence. Canadian banks generally require the ULC’s directors, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), and authorized signatories to complete a video-KYC interview. In practice, for a ULC without Canadian resident directors, the bank may mandate an in-person appointment at a branch or a notarized corroboration by a Canadian counsel. A registered Alberta office address, a Canadian-resident authorized agent, and a documented substance package materially accelerate onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC designation and foreign pass-through eligibility may trigger a 'transparent/opaque entity' classification review and increase scrutiny by Financial Crime Compliance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Certificate of Incorporation or Amalgamation; certified corporate by-laws and unanimous shareholder agreement; a board resolution naming authorized account signatories; full register of directors and shareholders; an up-to-date UBO declaration; and an Alberta counsel legal opinion confirming the ULC’s corporate and tax classification for Canadian purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue concentration in third-party payment aggregators (Stripe, Apple IAP) with high-volume, low-value cross-border transactions may be viewed as 'payment laundering' or failing to identify underlying customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant service agreements with Stripe and Apple; platform settlement statements and reconciliation trail; a documented compliance policy for end-customer verification; audited financial statements or management accounts; and a detailed business model narrative evidencing genuine software-as-a-service activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, unlimited liability structure, and expected cross-border wires to/from foreign jurisdictions may be flagged as a conduit or liquidity drain risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds declaration executed for all equity injections; FATCA/CRS self-certification forms for each UBO; shareholder loan or subscription agreements; an organizational chart demonstrating substantive Canadian business presence; and evidence of active software product development and customer contracts originating from Alberta.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical office or Canadian-resident director may trigger a 'mailbox company' or 'shell' assessment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta registered office lease arrangement; corporate records office appointment; detailed corporate substance narrative including key principals; Canadian business bank references or letters of introduction; and a financial forecast illustrating employment and operational expenditures in Canada.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan from a non-resident parent is executed via SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the ULC’s Schedule I operating account. The remittance instruction must carry a permitted purpose code (e.g., 'G220 - Other investment in Canadian equity' for capital contributions, or 'G110 - Foreign direct investment in Canada - Equity' as applicable under Statistics Canada’s classification). Verification by the receiving bank will include the corporate resolution authorizing the transaction, signed subscription agreement, and a UBO certificate demonstrating that the source of funds is lawful. For amounts equal to or exceeding CAD $10,000, the bank must issue an EFT report to FINTRAC. All funds are received in CAD or USD and immediately credited to the ULC’s operational liquidity pool; no conversion restriction applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for software royalties, external R&D services, and intercompany cost-sharing are cleared through SWIFT MT103 over the LVTS or the US-based Fedwire/CHIPS networks, depending on currency. For USD disbursements, the ULC should maintain a corresponding USD account at the Canadian bank for cheaper us-$ clearing. Commercial letters of credit are not required for intangible digital services; however, where goods-based hardware reselling exists, an irrevocable Documentary Credit may be opened at the financing bank. All outbound wires must include a compliant purpose code (e.g., '6810 - Software license fees', '4200 - Royalties', '2530 - Professional services'). FINTRAC EFT reporting thresholds and OFSI sanctions screening apply to beneficiary banks. CAD settlements are final and irrevocable through the LVTS, while USD settlements through Fedwire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank or federally authorized derivatives dealer, documented under a 1992 or 2002 ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex, for firm monthly cash-flow hedging.
FX swaps (spot-next/rollover swaps) for alteration of settlement dates, permitted under Bank Act derivative powers and exempt from mandatory clearing for commercial end-users.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) involving emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) with a CAD or USD deliverable leg, executed with an OSFI-regulated dealer and subject to FINTRAC record-keeping.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between CAD and USD to hedge both currency and interest-rate risk on long-term shareholder debt, cleared or non-cleared per OSFI guidelines, and documented under ISDA/CSA.

Foreign exchange options (CANAMEX style) are permissible but are intentionally excluded from the core treasury hedging program to reduce premium costs; if used, they must be executed with a licensed bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000 c. B-9)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the corporation's registration or incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty CAD 100 (approximately USD 75); failure to file for two consecutive years may prompt administrative dissolution by the Registrar after written notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return including Alberta provincial corporate income tax schedules and Schedule 50 Shareholder Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end, e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; CRA may impose repeated-filing penalties and pursue director liability for unremitted amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Register Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (filed as a component of the Alberta Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 60 days of the registration anniversary, concurrent with the Alberta Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance fines up to CAD 200,000 for individuals and CAD 500,000 for corporations; share transfers not recorded in the ISC Register within 15 days of knowledge trigger the same penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a private, non-publicly listed Alberta ULC; an audit becomes mandatory only if shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares make a written demand, the corporation is publicly listed or subject to a regulated sector mandate, or a court order is granted to a creditor or interested party
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for public reporting entities; a private Alberta ULC may adopt Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under CPA Canada Handbook Part II, with IFRS also permitted

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Alberta Corporate Transparency Rules (SA 2021 c. 17), the corporation must maintain an ISC Register and confirm that register with the Corporate Registry when filing its annual return; every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and the ISC Register within 15 days after the transfer is reported
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 400 per year in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 12,000 per year for a certified audit, if triggered

stage_6.triggering_act: Wilfully evading tax by false revenue understatement, fictitious expenses, destroying books, or misstating stock option/income
stage_6.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239(1) – indictable offence with fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; CRA can re-assess beyond normal period (s.152(7) if misrepresentation); revoke tax registration.
stage_6.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/officers can be charged as parties if they deliberately participated; CRA s.227.1 imposes joint liability on directors for unremitted withholdings; ULC shareholders with unlimited liability may also face direct creditor claims.
